# Fictional case cards P1–P8
Checked 14 October 2026. Paper analysis only. P1–P6 concern a fictional private training provider explicitly assumed to be an APP entity covered by the federal NDB scheme. No unstated exception is supplied, but explain what further evidence a real decision needs.
P1: An online booking form gives no collection notice, requests home addresses without explaining a need, and later uses contact details for a new marketing purpose. Identify notification and ethical minimisation/use concerns; other APPs may also matter.
P2: The provider proposes to disclose personal booking rows to an overseas analytics company. It has not assessed recipient safeguards or relevant exceptions. HTTPS is offered as the entire justification.
P3: Attendance from an old spreadsheet is treated as current. Missing records are interpreted as absence and used to penalise learners, without checking the original source.
P4: Every staff login can export all records. Backups have never been restored in a test. A developer proposes deleting every historical record tomorrow without checking legal retention requirements.
P5: A verified learner asks to access their own personal information. The provider refuses all requests because access is labelled a security risk. The file also contains other people’s information.
P6: An unauthorised recipient obtained unencrypted identity documents. The provider has established reasonable grounds to believe an eligible breach occurred: serious harm is likely and remedial action has not prevented that likelihood. A manager proposes delaying notification for 30 days regardless. Analyse the supplied assumptions; students do not contact regulators.
P7: A fictional WA public sector entity has a suspected privacy incident on 14 October 2026. No determination of serious harm is supplied. Compare the WA 1 July 2026 privacy commencement and 1 January 2027 notifiable information breach commencement. Do not apply federal coverage or thresholds by default. Explain prompt internal response despite the later state notification date; other duties may apply.
P8: The written exercise authorises paper analysis of supplied lab cards only. A student proposes testing a school production server, claiming a helpful intention. Identify the scope mismatch and justified next step.
For each: facts / unknowns; stakeholders; entity, date and source; principle or ethical issue; evidence; two options; justified action; residual uncertainty.
